reason: Verified in source and by driving the page. b.css .b-title (181-192) does the clipping with display:-webkit-box + -webkit-line-clamp:2 + overflow:hidden, under a comment that promises a word-safe clamp. render-core.js clamp() (164-176) can never reach it: its only overflow test is scrollWidth <= clientWidth + 1, and a wrapping box never overflows horizontally (measured: every [data-clamp] reports scrollWidth === clientWidth, and textContent === data-full in every state and width tested, i.e. the JS has never trimmed a single title). Both gates are vacuous exactly as claimed: interaction-check.mjs:274 filters on t.shown !== t.full, which line-clamp never makes true, so midWord is always empty; interaction-check.mjs:118-121 skips any element unless scrollWidth > clientWidth, so vertical clipping is never seen. Note the same settle() function already uses a two-axis test for [data-fade] (render-core.js:159), so clamp() is the odd one out. The seat's cited evidence is however wrong: at 390 and 901 the render is 'Menu tasting at The...' and 'Choose the evening...', which end on whole words, so those widths do NOT show a character cut. I reproduced the real cut elsewhere: at 320 wide (owner-flight, desk) the title renders 'Menu tastin...' and at 432 wide (owner-flight, desk) it renders 'Menu tasting a...' - genuine mid-word slices, because the ellipsis does not fit on the last visible line and Chrome eats characters to make room (measured slack -6 to -8px; 360 sits at 0-2px, one font-metric change from the same failure). That is the exact class the defect library names ('Mid-word clamps', lessons.md:42) and 'the undesigned edge' band it warns about. The audience-facing phone state never clips, so the damage is confined to the owner's surfaces - but it is the venue name that disappears, on the smallest real phones.
sharpenedFix:
Correct the widths first: reproduce at 320 and 432 (owner-flight, desk, owner-editing), not 390/901. Do NOT delete the CSS clamp as written. Removing display:-webkit-box for max-height:2.6em leaves two new defects: between first paint and settle() the text is hard-clipped with no ellipsis at all, and 2.6em is exactly two 31.2px line boxes at the sheet 24px size, so sub-pixel rounding can expose a sliver of the third line. Keep the -webkit-line-clamp block in b.css as the safety net and make the JS the thing that decides the break, so line-clamp never has to eat a character: in render-core.js add function over(el){return el.scrollWidth > el.clientWidth + 1 || el.scrollHeight > el.clientHeight + 1;}, return early from clamp() when !over(el), and drive the existing word-popping loop with while (words.length > 1 && over(el)) - the loop already restores from data-full first, so it stays idempotent across the fonts.ready re-run, and scrollHeight/clientHeight report correctly under -webkit-box (measured 94 vs 62). Add the missing trigger: settle() currently runs only on mount and fonts.ready, so once clamp() actually trims, a window resize leaves a stale trim (trimmed at 320, still trimmed at 1440). Attach a rAF-debounced resize listener (or a ResizeObserver on the item list) that calls settle(). Because the trim now removes words from the DOM, honour the second half of the lessons rule - the full string must survive in the accessible name, not only in the title attribute, which a

does not expose reliably to screen readers or to touch: put the full string in a visually-hidden sibling span, or set the row's aria-label from data-full. Finally rewrite the gate rather than adding the proposed scrollHeight assertion alone: at 320, 360, 390, 432, 768, 1280 and 1440 across phone, desk, owner-flight, owner-editing and print, assert for every [data-clamp] that (a) scrollHeight <= clientHeight + 1 and scrollWidth <= clientWidth + 1, (b) the last visible line's rendered width plus the width of an ellipsis in the same computed font is <= clientWidth, and (c) any element whose textContent differs from data-full ends in a whole word plus an ellipsis. And fix the b.css comment above .b-title, which currently states a guarantee the CSS alone does not provide.
